## Customer concentration

Over the trailing 12 months (2025-07-01 to 2026-07-01, basis: invoice amounts issued), our largest customer is **Baylor Foods (CU-0007)** at **38.0%** of total invoiced revenue ($464,762 of the period's invoices). The next four largest customers each account for only 5.8%. That is a high concentration: losing this one account would remove more revenue than our next four biggest customers combined.

## Do they pay on time

No. Terms are net-30, but looking at the 88 invoices from Baylor that have been paid in this window, every single one was late, averaging **32.1 days past due** (range 28-36 days), meaning they effectively take about 60 days to pay a 30-day invoice. That said, they are consistent: none of their invoices have crossed into the 61-90 or 90+ day buckets, so firm-wide receivables aging (as of 2026-07-01) shows nothing in 61-90 or 90+ (current: $107,666; 1-30 days: $38,956; nothing beyond that). Nothing on Baylor currently triggers the owner-escalation threshold (>90 days overdue) for a reminder.

One flag worth your attention: Baylor's stated credit limit in our system is only $12,700, but they currently have **$75,547 in open invoices outstanding** (16 open invoices), roughly 6x their limit. I did not place or lift any hold since none was requested, and per policy a hold on any of the five largest customers needs your explicit approval before it's applied. If you want, I can prepare a credit-limit review or a hold request for your approval, or send payment reminders on the open invoices that have passed their due date (8 of the 16, all under 30 days overdue, which the data team can send without escalation).

ANSWER: Our biggest customer, Baylor Foods, drives 38% of invoiced revenue over the trailing 12 months versus 5.8% each for the next four largest, so concentration risk is high. They pay reliably but consistently late, averaging 32 days past their 30-day terms, though none of their invoices have reached the 90-day escalation threshold; separately, their $75,547 in open invoices is about 6x their $12,700 credit limit, which may warrant a review.
